questions.name: q0
questions.instructions:
Are the identifiers in this function searchable with terms a developer would use to find this code?

Yes: The code identifiers judged here are those in the function's declaration and body - its own name, its parameters, its locals, and the names it reads - and they are greppable: written out in full at every occurrence, never split into fragments or dynamically constructed from pieces, never renamed at a boundary, and specific enough that a search hit is genuinely a reference to this thing.
No: At least one identifier in the function cannot be found by a single search: it is split into fragments or dynamically constructed from pieces, renamed at a boundary so the same concept needs two search strings, or is a bare word (data, handler, util) whose hits are mostly noise. CLI flag spellings, help text, and log messages are user-facing interface, not code identifiers, and are outside this rule.

questions.name: q1
questions.instructions:
Does this function's error handling lose information about the original failure?

Yes: Error handling loses information: a caught error is swallowed, rethrown without its cause, or replaced by a message that drops the original failure detail.
No: Error handling preserves information: causes are chained, messages include the original failure detail, and nothing is swallowed silently.

questions.name: q2
questions.instructions: How much EFFORT does a reader need to follow this code's logic - effort caused by structure the author chose, not by the problem itself? Ignore length alone: a long linear unit with one job reads as easy. Ignore inherent complexity: cases the data or the domain genuinely force are not this failure. Judge how hard the code's own structure makes it to read top-to-bottom.

levels.description: Easy: the logic reads top-to-bottom. A single pass suffices. Any difficulty present is inherent to the problem, not to the structure.

Moderate: the reader must pause once or twice - hold a small amount of state across a few lines, or re-check an outer condition - but the structure is otherwise linear and the full flow is recoverable by re-reading one or two spots.

Hard: following the code requires actively reconstructing its flow - a stack of nested conditions to track, several unrelated concerns fused into one unit, state held across many lines, or an order that forces jumps instead of top-to-bottom reading. The structural difficulty could be removed without changing what the code does.

questions.name: q3
questions.instructions:
Does this unit serve a single cohesive responsibility, every step serving one stated purpose?

Yes: The unit performs one cohesive responsibility: all its steps serve a single purpose its name and docblock state.
No: There is more than one reason for the unit to change: it mixes business logic, data validation, and side effects.
